topic: Ryan Figures It Out: the viral November 17 90-day blackout rumor

sources.title: Is 90-day blackout beginning Nov. 17? Why unfounded rumor is spreading (Snopes, Nov 16 2026)
sources.text: At 2:20 p.m. Eastern time Nov. 17, FEMA and the FCC plan to conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, announced in September. The claim gained traction due to a Microsoft Outlook outage Nov. 12, a nationwide aircraft ground stop Nov. 13 due to a failure in telecommunication infrastructure, and software outages at several major banks on Nov. 16. A 2023 Simpsons episode, 'It's a Blunderful Life', aired Nov. 19, 2023, featured a blackout starting Nov. 17, six days before Thanksgiving; in 2023 Thanksgiving fell on Nov. 23, in 2026 Thanksgiving is on Nov. 26. FEMA is required by law to conduct a nationwide EAS test at least once every three years; the last occurred Oct. 4, 2023. FEMA will not be testing cellphone alerts this time; backup test Dec. 3.

sources.title: Is there a blackout on November 17? No. The date belongs to a one-minute TV and radio alert test (Nacionale)
sources.text: No government or power company has announced a blackout for November 17. The Emergency Alert System test interrupts TV and radio for about a minute starting at 2:20 p.m. ET and does not touch the power grid (FCC notice DA-26-989, Sept 16). Radio and TV stations, cable and satellite TV and satellite radio must carry it, in English and Spanish, with the line 'This is only a test. No action is required by the public.' The test does not include Wireless Emergency Alerts. Rumor sources: a viral X post around November 1 about a Simpsons episode; the real alert test; preparedness advice such as the UK 'Be Ready' campaign and Brazil's Civil Defense urging about three days of water and food; the U.S. military FORTRESS program announced September 30 to give bases 90 days of power, water and fuel; a '33 countries' Newsweek map of governments that give stockpiling advice. Grids are run separately by country and region.

sources.title: Is a 90-day blackout coming? What the U.S. military's new readiness initiative actually means (WBBJ/Gray News, Nov 5 2026)
sources.text: The rumor began circulating after U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth unveiled a long-term strategic plan on Sept. 30. The FORTRESS America initiative is not an announcement of an active blackout; it is a plan so the military can 'fight and win under any circumstances,' including a cyberattack. It is organized around five pillars: energy independence, supply-chain and defense-industrial base resilience, a strategic defense reserve, installation hardening and cyber resilience, and resilience in space and spectrum. Every military department and defense agency will have the ability to operate independently for at least 90 days, including water, electricity, fuel and communications.

sources.title: Has the US ever had a nationwide blackout? No. (Nacionale)
sources.text: The United States has never had a blackout that took out power across the whole country at once. The Lower 48 states run on three main interconnections: the Eastern Interconnection, the Western Interconnection and the Texas grid run by ERCOT. 1965 (Nov 9): more than 30 million people, a faulty relay at the Sir Adam Beck plant in Ontario. 2003 (Aug 14): an estimated 50 million people, a high-voltage line in northern Ohio sagged into trees and tripped without the utility realizing it. 2021 (February): more than 4.5 million Texans, a winter storm froze power plants and gas supplies.

sources.title: How do you prepare for a power outage? (Nacionale citing CDC and FEMA)
sources.text: One gallon of water per person per day for at least three days and nonperishable food for at least three days (FEMA/Ready.gov). CDC: never run a generator inside a home, basement or garage, even with doors and windows open; keep it at least 20 feet from any window, door or vent. About 4 hours in the fridge with the door closed; a full freezer about 48 hours, half-full about 24 hours. Use battery-powered flashlights and lanterns rather than candles.
